## What this document does

One row per participant × target sentence (5 Polio and 5 TB target sentences, each
containing the answer to one question; `R/data.R`). Durations are in s/word (the models'
scale; the manuscript reports ms/word). Measures and models:

| Measure | Family (link) | Prior SD *s* of every pairwise difference |
|---|---|---|
| Total gaze duration | ex-Gaussian (`cogmod::cogmod_exgaussian`; μ identity, σ and τ softplus); Status/Group and Topic on μ and τ | μ: 0.1 s/word; τ: 0.5 |
| Re-reading time (after moving on to later text; sentences re-read only) | Gamma (log) | 0.5 |
| Regression-in (look-back: returned to from later text, 0/1) | Bernoulli (logit) | 1.5 |
| First-pass reading: selective regression-path duration | ex-Gaussian, as for total gaze duration | μ: 0.1 s/word; τ: 0.5 |

Two sets of models, as for the final test: **status models** (Prequestioned,
Non-prequestioned, no-prequestion + Topic; comparisons with no-prequestion) and **Group × Topic models**
(Polio − TB within each group, and the interaction contrast; for look-backs, their Bayes factors are on the response scale, the scale of the estimates). Random
effects: the maximal structure warranted by the design, by-participant intercepts and
Topic slopes and by-sentence intercepts and Status (or Group) slopes (every sentence was
read in all three statuses and by all three groups).
Equal-prior contrasts, Savage–Dickey Bayes factors from `modelbased` comparisons, and
cached fits as described in `R/bayes_helpers.R`.

**Why cogmod only for total gaze duration.** cogmod's ex-Gaussian is the classical μ, σ, τ
parameterisation, as preregistered. cogmod's other duration families are response-time
models (e.g. `cogmod_gamma()` is a shifted Gamma parameterised by shape and scale), whose
parameters are not mean reading time. Re-reading time uses brms's mean-parameterised Gamma, so its effects are effects on mean
reading time. The ex-Gaussian could not be estimated for re-reading time (σ collapsed: many
single brief fixations).

**First-pass reading time.** The preregistered first-pass duration (from first entering
the sentence until first leaving it) is bimodal: about half of first passes are cut short
after a few fixations by a brief return to the preceding line, so it mixes complete first
readings (median about 3 s) with interrupted ones (median about 0.4 s), and no single
distribution (ex-Gaussian, Gamma, lognormal) describes it. First-pass reading is
therefore measured as selective regression-path duration (`go_past`; Schotter & Dillon, 2025): fixations on the sentence from
first entering it until the reader first moves on to later text, so brief returns to
earlier text do not end it and time spent on earlier text is not counted. Its distribution
is unimodal and the ex-Gaussian describes it closely, so it is analysed like total gaze
duration (μ and τ). The model key remains `first_pass`.

*Naming:* the paper calls the group without prequestions the **no-prequestion** condition; in the data and code it is labelled `Control`.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(here)
fit_settings <- list(chains = 4, iter = 11000, warmup = 1000, adapt_delta = 0.95, refit = FALSE)
if (exists("params")) {
  fit_settings <- modifyList(fit_settings, params[intersect(names(params), names(fit_settings))])
}
source(here("R", "setup.R"))
source(here("R", "data.R"))
source(here("R", "bayes_helpers.R"))
```

## Data

```{r}
#| label: data
# Durations in s/word; re-reading time is NA for sentences not re-read after the reader
# moved on (whether they were re-read is the look-back measure)
et <- dat_status |>
  mutate(first_pass = go_past,   # first-pass reading = selective regression-path duration
         across(c(total_fix, first_pass, reread_time), \(x) x / 1000)) |>
  select(participant, sentence, condition, topic, status,
         total_fix, first_pass, reread_time, regressed_in)
et_dv <- \(dv) equal_prior(droplevels(et[!is.na(et[[dv]]), ]))
et_dv_cond <- \(dv) cond_coding(et_dv(dv))

count(et, status, topic)
```

## Models

```{r}
#| label: fit
#| results: hide
m_et <- list(
  total_fix = fit_brm(
    bf(as.formula(paste("total_fix ~ status + topic +", re_et)),
       sigma ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
       as.formula(paste("tau ~ status + topic +", re_et))),
    et_dv("total_fix"),
    cogmod_exgaussian(),   # cogmod's default links: identity for mu, softplus for sigma and tau
    pr_exg, "bayes_status_total_fix", stanvars = cogmod_exgaussian_stanvars()),
  reread_time = fit_brm(as.formula(paste("reread_time ~ status + topic +", re_et)),
                        et_dv("reread_time"), Gamma(link = "log"), pr_gamma,
                        "bayes_status_reread_after"),
  regressed_in = fit_brm(as.formula(paste("regressed_in ~ status + topic +", re_et)),
                         et_dv("regressed_in"), bernoulli(), pr_logit, "bayes_status_regressed_in"),
  first_pass = fit_brm(
    bf(as.formula(paste("first_pass ~ status + topic +", re_et)),
       sigma ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
       as.formula(paste("tau ~ status + topic +", re_et))),
    et_dv("first_pass"), cogmod_exgaussian(), pr_exg, "bayes_status_go_past_exg",
    stanvars = cogmod_exgaussian_stanvars())
)

m_topic <- list(
  total_fix = fit_brm(
    bf(as.formula(paste("total_fix ~ condition * topic +", re_et_cond)),
       sigma ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
       as.formula(paste("tau ~ condition * topic +", re_et_cond))),
    et_dv_cond("total_fix"), cogmod_exgaussian(), pr_exg, "bayes_cond_topic_total_fix",
    stanvars = cogmod_exgaussian_stanvars()),
  reread_time = fit_brm(as.formula(paste("reread_time ~ condition * topic +", re_et_cond)),
                        et_dv_cond("reread_time"), Gamma(link = "log"), pr_gamma,
                        "bayes_cond_topic_reread_after"),
  regressed_in = fit_brm(as.formula(paste("regressed_in ~ condition * topic +", re_et_cond)),
                         et_dv_cond("regressed_in"), bernoulli(), pr_logit,
                         "bayes_cond_topic_regressed_in"),
  first_pass = fit_brm(
    bf(as.formula(paste("first_pass ~ condition * topic +", re_et_cond)),
       sigma ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
       as.formula(paste("tau ~ condition * topic +", re_et_cond))),
    et_dv_cond("first_pass"), cogmod_exgaussian(), pr_exg, "bayes_cond_topic_go_past_exg",
    stanvars = cogmod_exgaussian_stanvars())
)
```

## Diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: diagnostics
diag_tab <- diag_table(c(m_et, set_names(m_topic, paste0(names(m_topic), " (Group × Topic)"))))
diag_tab
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
patchwork::wrap_plots(imap(m_et, \(m, nm) pp_check(m, ndraws = 50) + labs(title = nm)), ncol = 2)
```

## Status models: prequestioned and non-prequestioned vs. no-prequestion

Bayes factors on the link scale (τ and the expected re-reading time on the response
scale, the latter at the population level); estimates on the response scale.

```{r}
#| label: status
bf_tab <- bf_table(m_et)
est_tab <- contrasts_by(m_et)
means_tab <- means_by(m_et, "status")
means_draws <- mean_draws_by(m_et, "status")
bf_tab |> transmute(model, parameter, comparison, BF10, BF01) |> kable(digits = 2)
est_tab
```

## Group × Topic

```{r}
#| label: group-topic
# look-backs (a probability): Bayes factors on the response scale, the scale of the estimates
bf_topic_tab <- bf_table(m_topic, topic_draws, response_scale = "regressed_in")
est_topic_tab <- topic_estimates(m_topic)
means_topic_tab <- means_by(m_topic, c("condition", "topic")) |> add_status()
means_topic_draws <- mean_draws_by(m_topic, c("condition", "topic")) |> add_status()
bf_topic_tab |> transmute(model, parameter, comparison, BF10, BF01) |> kable(digits = 2)
est_topic_tab
```

## Prior sensitivity

```{r}
#| label: priorsense
sens_tab <- sens_table(c(m_et, set_names(m_topic, paste0(names(m_topic), " (Group × Topic)"))))
sens_tab
```

## Results file

```{r}
#| label: save-results
save_results(list(diag = diag_tab, bf = bf_tab, est = est_tab, means = means_tab,
                  means_draws = means_draws, bf_topic = bf_topic_tab, est_topic = est_topic_tab,
                  means_topic = means_topic_tab, means_topic_draws = means_topic_draws,
                  sens = sens_tab,
                  n_draws = nrow(posterior::as_draws_df(m_et$first_pass))),
             here("analysis", "results_eye_tracking.rds"))
```
